title: Feathers and Fences
goals: Build the Sawmill or the Smokehouse
reward: 1,000g, a recruit and 250 Farm Rank points
source: CS43; F27 decisions 12 and 13 (the beats), scripted here as the prototype

scenes.title: Two Hens in a Crate
outline: Dale Hart’s wagon at the Gate, two hens in a crate
He raises a coop beside the Fields and settles them in; your best rancher takes them on
Feed: Chicken Feed from the shop, one a night each; “a hungry hen lays nothing”
Care: one carer to a pen of four, the same hands day after day; hearts make better eggs
Marta stocks feed; the Mayor reads the goals card

beats.line: A wagon rattles up to the Gate. Two hens peer out of a crate in the back.
“Dale Hart, from the ranch over the hill. The Mayor said you’d have room for two hens.”
“No coop yet? Then we’ll raise one. Lend me a morning and a few strong hands.”
By noon a little coop stands beside the Fields, and the hens step out to look around.
“Leave them to me. I’ll learn every feather.”
“Feed each hen one Chicken Feed a night. A hungry hen lays nothing.”
“Give a pen of four one carer, and keep the same hands on it, day after day.”
“Hens lay for someone they know. Win their hearts and the eggs get better.”
“I’ve put Chicken Feed on my shelves, ten gold a bag. I’ll keep it stocked.”
“A coop already! Here’s what the town hopes to see next.”

scenes.title: A Full Coop
outline: A full coop at dawn, and a heavy egg basket
Dale says the farm is ready for a barn, and gives you his old cowbell
Your newest hand at the Gate
The Mayor mentions Gus Talbot, a retired miner, and the boarded-up Mine; chapter 3 Soon

beats.line: Dawn. Four hens fuss in a full coop, and the egg basket is heavy.
“Look at that. You’ve a knack for this, all of you.”
“A farm that keeps hens can keep cows. Put up a barn and I’ll bring you the rest.”
“Here, take my old cowbell. It’s rung over every herd I ever started.”
A visitor walks in at the Gate.
“I’m {name}. Word is this farm keeps hens now. Is there room for one more hand?”
“Have you met Gus Talbot? He ran the old Mine before it was boarded up.”
“He says the hill still has iron in it. He might show you, if you ask him nicely.”
